patches.from: In ex8-6-21c, $AB\parallel DC$ (both gradient $0$) is true and is the book's first fact — but the book then also compares the lengths of the other pair of opposite sides, $AD$ and $BC$, and finds them equal; only that second check earns 'isosceles.' Stopping after the parallel check alone gives 'trapezium'; assuming the other pair must also be parallel because it's equal in length gives 'parallelogram' — but $m_{AD}=4$ and $m_{BC}=-4$ are not equal, so that pair is not parallel.
patches.to: For the quadrilateral with $A(0, 3)$, $B(4, 3)$, $C(5, -1)$ and $D(-1, -1)$, $AB\parallel DC$ (both gradient $0$) is true and is the book's first fact — but the book then also compares the lengths of the other pair of opposite sides, $AD$ and $BC$, and finds them equal; only that second check earns 'isosceles.' Stopping after the parallel check alone gives 'trapezium'; assuming the other pair must also be parallel because it's equal in length gives 'parallelogram' — but $m_{AD}=4$ and $m_{BC}=-4$ are not equal, so that pair is not parallel.

patches.from: In ex8-6-36b, showing $m_{MP}\times m_{LN}=-1$ (diagonals perpendicular) proves $LMNP$ is a rhombus — true, but only half the picture; the book goes on to also show $LM\perp MN$, and only combining both facts earns 'square.' The book's own review note on ex8-6-42e makes the same point explicitly: 'rectangle', 'rhombus' and 'kite' are 'also true, less precisely' — not wrong, just not the finished answer.
patches.to: For the parallelogram $LMNP$ with $L(-1, -1)$, $M(-2, 4)$ and $P(4, 0)$, showing $m_{MP}\times m_{LN}=-1$ (diagonals perpendicular) proves $LMNP$ is a rhombus — true, but only half the picture; it takes a right angle as well, $LM\perp MN$, to earn 'square'. A square is also a rectangle, a rhombus and a kite, so those names are true, just less precise — not wrong, just not the finished answer.
